Module–Trait Association — Frontal Cortex (Bulk RNA-seq)

Extended Analysis: Age, FTD/AD Comorbidity, Site of Motor Onset

ALS Deconvolution Project

2026-04-28

What this analysis adds: The original WGCNA module–trait analysis included only four traits: ALS status, sex, RIN (RNA quality), and C9ORF72 expansion status. This extended analysis adds three new trait categories:

  • Age at Death — Tests whether any co-expression module is correlated with subject age, which could confound ALS associations.
  • FTD/AD Comorbidity — A binary indicator (1 = present, 0 = absent) flagging any subject whose Subject.Group.Subcategory mentions Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) or Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). This captures the subset of ALS patients with concurrent neurodegeneration.
  • Site of Motor Onset — Three binary indicator columns encoding the canonical onset region:
    • Onset_Limb: includes Limb, Lower/Upper Limb, Lower/Upper Extremity, Upper and Lower Limbs, combined entries (e.g., “Bulbar and Limb”), and Generalized.
    • Onset_Bulbar: includes Bulbar, combined entries, and Generalized.
    • Onset_Axial: includes Axial, combined entries, and Generalized.
    • Rows with “Not Applicable”, “Unknown”, blank, or “Dementia onset” receive 0 for all three columns.

Filtering rationale (Section 4): A module is retained only if its ALS p-value < 0.05 (significantly associated with ALS) and its RIN p-value > 0.05 (not significantly associated with RNA quality). This independence filter ensures that ALS-correlated modules are not simply capturing differences in tissue quality.

Dataset: Frontal Cortex — Bulk RNA-seq  |  Retained samples: 116  |  Non-grey modules: 77

4 ALS Association Direction — Bar Graph

For each filtered module, bars show −log₁₀(ALS p-value) × sign(ALS correlation). Positive bars = module up-regulated in ALS; negative bars = module down-regulated in ALS. The dashed lines mark the p = 0.05 threshold.

5 Summary & Brief Analysis

10 module(s) survived the dual filter in the Frontal Cortex: 0 up-regulated and 10 down-regulated in ALS, independent of RNA quality.

Key observations:

  • Modules passing this filter show a genuine ALS-associated transcriptional signature in bulk frontal cortex tissue, not explained by differential RNA degradation (RIN).
  • Additional traits (Age, FTD/AD comorbidity, Site of Motor Onset) reveal whether these modules also associate with disease heterogeneity — a module correlated with both ALS and bulbar onset, for instance, may reflect distinct disease biology.
  • Modules correlated with FTD/AD comorbidity should be interpreted cautiously, as they may reflect mixed neurodegeneration rather than pure ALS biology.
